tier_rationale: Manufacturer product page describes knob/electronic hybrid controls with preset cycles and a moisture sensor, and lists no WiFi, app, or connectivity feature anywhere. FCC grantee search on the manufacturer (Alliance Laundry Systems, grantee code 2ANOT) confirms the sibling control: this vendor does file wireless grants when a product has a radio (commercial network gateways, a WiFi network controller, an NFC control panel) but none of its nine grants name the DC5 or any residential dryer.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes. You turn a knob to a cycle, set the temperature, and press start. There is no Wi-Fi, no app, no account, and no cloud step in drying a load of laundry. The moisture sensor and steam-refresh cycle are onboard electronics, not connected features — they work exactly the same with the router unplugged as with it running.

repairability.notes: Commercial-derived platform sold through the same dealer network as Speed Queen's laundromat machines, with the same 5-year full parts and labour warranty. Serviced by appliance technicians rather than board swaps.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: model DC5004WE (internal code ADE6ARYS177TW01), knob/electronic hybrid controls, 6 preset cycles, 4 temperature selections, moisture sensor, steam refresh, $1,649 MSRP, 5-year parts and labour warranty. No WiFi, app, or connectivity feature listed anywhere on the page; only a separate warranty-registration link, not an account system.

FCC grant list for Alliance Laundry Systems LLC (Speed Queen's manufacturer, grantee 2ANOT): 9 grants, all for commercial connected-laundry hardware (a WiFi network controller system, wireless network control modules, an NFC USB control panel, network gateways — models MC10 and M8000UFL). None of the 9 grants name the DC5 or any residential dryer, establishing the sibling control that this vendor files when a product has a radio.

open_questions: No teardown or internal photos of the DC5004WE found to confirm the absence of a radio directly — the FCC absence is inferred from grantee-level filing behaviour, not from a grant search on the exact model.

Confirm whether Speed Queen's residential line has any plan to add the commercial 'Speed Queen Insights' connectivity module to the DC5 in future model years; if so this record would need re-verification.
notes: Pairs with the already-catalogued speed-queen-tc5003wn washer. Same manufacturer, same commercial-derived design philosophy, same evidence pattern: the residential Classic line stays mechanical while the manufacturer's connectivity investment goes entirely into commercial laundromat hardware (payment systems, remote monitoring for operators) that operators want and homeowners do not.
